overall_reason: The system UI stack (Segoe UI drew every glyph at 1440 per fonts.json; system-ui computed at 375) sets every role, which fits a product-UI (Operate) composition on the same 14/12px ladder as a plain deploy card, but the head is filled with a gradient and every role is tinted violet, so the head is the only text that does not read as solid type.

score.reason: T-HEAD-TREATMENT fails (the head has a gradient fill), and T-LADDER fails on the 14px/600 head against 14px/500 rows.

findings.title: Headings are set in one voice
findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json 'Recent deploys' has color rgba(0,0,0,0), which means a clipped background gradient paints it. On P48/01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png the head runs from violet to pink. The row titles are solid rgb(76,29,149).
findings.after: Set the head in one solid ink, the same one as the row titles, and carry its rank by size or weight
findings.why: A gradient fill makes the head a decoration rather than a label, and it has no single contrast value to check.

findings.title: Weight steps are clear
findings.where: Card head and row titles, 1440 and 375
findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json the head 'Recent deploys' is 14px/600 and the row titles 'Checkout redesign', 'Search speedup' and 'Pricing copy' are 14px/500. The head and the rows have the same size, and only a 100-weight step separates them. On P48/01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png the head reads no stronger than the rows.
findings.after: Separate the head from the rows by size (head 15 to 16px, or rows 13px), or by a clear weight step (400 against 600 or 700)
findings.why: A 500-to-600 step at the same size looks like a rendering difference, so the card has no clear entry point.

strengths: Sizes and leading match a consistent 14/12px ladder, and nothing is tracked or set in caps.
not_investigated: T-MEASURE: no paragraph of 3 or more lines at either width
Size floors under 12px (A11-002) and contrast belong to the sweep and the color lens; not repeated here
The violet tint on meta text (rgb(167,139,250)) is a contrast question for the color lens and the sweep
